audits.title: Eradication of brucella melitensis in sheep and goats

recommendations.text: Recommendations for the Greek Competent Authorities concerning the eradication programme for the next year · A new control/eradication programme should be elaborated. This programme should begin only when agreement has been achieved relating to the availability of finance, personnel, laboratory capacities, vaccines and an efficient movement control system. This programme should be drafted in agreement with the health authorities and the farmer associations. · In selected areas preliminary field trials on the conjunctival method should be conducted in adult sheep and goats and the results should carefully be evaluated before a mass vaccination programme can be launched. · An immediate public health warning should be instituted to advise the Greeks and tourists on the risks and hazards related to Brucella melitensis infection, especially in relation to cheese produced on the farms on a small scale.

Recommendations for the European Commission · The Payment which has taken place for the 1997 Ovine and Caprine Brucellosis Eradication Programme in Greece should be reconsidered. · Ewe premia and future financial support for the transportation of sheep and goats intended for transhumance should only be given to owners whose flocks are engaged in the Control and Eradication Programme. · An inquiry should be pursued to eliminate the possibility of double financing of the Greek Brucellosis Eradication Programme under veterinary and structural funds having taken place in the years 1992 to 1995. · The opinion of the Scientific Veterinary Committee should be requested concerning - the advantages, in terms of public health protection, of mass vaccination of adult sheep and goats. - the value of the serological tests actually employed in the eradication of Brucella melitensis in sheep and goats. 9

The Commission services should examine the situation with a view to opening legal proceedings against Greece for non-enforcement of the rules laid down by Directive 91/628/EEC and Directive 93/119/EEC. 8.2. Another Commission mission to Greece should be carried out after 30.6.1999 to verify progress in the various veterinary fields described in this mission report. n 9

audits.title: Fresh meat establishments, trade and animal identification

recommendations.text: Slaughter hygiene: The authorities should take action to ensure that the slaughter hygiene fulfils the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC.

Protection of animals at the time of slaughter: The authorities should take action to ensure that the shortcomings in regard to animal welfare at the time of slaughter are corrected immediately to meet the provisions of Council Directive 93/119/EEC.

Health marking: The authorities should take action to ensure that the shortcomings in regard to health marking are corrected immediately to meet the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC. · Any outstanding action planned or taken, to be completed within a maximum deadline of six months, addressing the followi s:.

Approval procedures: The authorities should take action to ensure that the requirements for approval of establishments are being continuously fulfilled after initial approval and fully meet the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC. All the approved establishment should be re-evaluated and corrective measures, combined with a strict timetable, implemented.

Veterinary supervision: ­ The authorities should take action to ensure that veterinary presence in establishments fulfils the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC. Serious efforts should be made to recruit and train the necessary staff. ­ The authorities should take action to ensure that a veterinary supervision is performed that leads to correction of individual differences between establishments and Nomi and fulfils the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC. ­ The authorities should take action to ensure that "Own checks" to be carried out by the management of establishments in combination with a HACCP approach, and the control thereof by the Official Veterinarian, meet the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC. Page 19 of 20
Veterinary control on Slaughter hygiene: The authorities should take action to ensure that veterinary supervision of the slaughter hygiene fulfils the provisions of Council Directive 64/433/EEC
Training of personnel: Training should be organised by the management with involvement of the official veterinarian responsible for the plant in the planning and implementation.
Training of the veterinary staff: Training should be organised for the official veterinarian responsible for the plants and their supervisors.

Animal identification: The authorities should take action to adopt the proposal of the amended legislation regarding animal identification and to ensure it's implementation in order to fulfil the provisions of Council Directive 92/102/EEC and Council Regulation 820/97/EEC as appropriate and Commission Regulations 2628/97/EC, 2629/97/EC, 2630/97/EC and 494/98/EC.

Traceability & Trade documentation: Greater emphasis should be put on the development of systems, which allow a better traceability. 12 RECOMMENDATION FOR ACTION BY THE COMMISSION SERVICES. ­ The relevant authorities of Greece should be asked to carry out improvements concerning the subjects mentioned in Chapter 10, and to provide information on the improvements within a defined time. ­ In addition, serious consideration should be given to legal proceedings being taken against Greece on the grounds that the veterinary supervision does not guarantee that the provisions of the Council Directive 64/433/EEC, in particular approval and operational requirements, are met in all slaughterhouses and cutting plants. ­ In addition, consideration should be given to legal proceedings being taken against Greece because of the fact that identification of bovine animals is not in accordance with the provisions of Council Directive 92/102/EEC and Council Regulation 820/97/EC as appropriate and Commission Regulations 2628/97/EC, 2629/97/EC, 2630/97/EC and 494//98/EC. ­ Considering the significance of the findings of this and previous missions, covering the same but also different subjects and considering the lack of positive evolution during the last years, it is strongly recommended to elaborate a global strategy for Greece to tackle the problems encountered. audits.title: Bluetongue in cattle, sheep and goats

recommendations.text: To the national veterinary authority of Greece: It is recommended : the establishment and maintenance of the surveillance plan outlined in this report; that consideration be given to the effect of lack of staff on all aspects of the work of the veterinary services but particularly on the question of staff training and supervision; that development continue on the EVROS computer system as a weapon in the fight against exotic disease; that a contingency plan be developed for the entire country based on the surveillance programme discussed above.

To the Services of the European Commission: It is recommended : a revision of Council Directives 92/119/EEC and 90/425/EEC to include measures specifically related to bluetongue; the establishment of a detailed study of the possible risks to human and animal health of incursions of vector-borne diseases into southern Member States; consideration of possible approaches to the veterinary authorities in any country or countries likely to be the source of infective Culicoides with a view to joint action to protect European Union territory from future incursions. 12

recommendations.text: It is recommended that the measures described in 5.6, while welcome, should be regarded as secondary to the institution of a vaccination programme throughout the area considered to be under threat.

Sampling procedure The inspectors should ensure that the incremental samples are taken from different points throughout a container in order to receive representative samples for the whole lot. This may include the unloading of containers, if some parts of the lot within the container are not accessible. The combined total amount of the incremental samples should be increased and brought in line with the requirements of Commission Directive 98/53/EC, which will become obligatory by 1 January 2001.

Laboratory services visited Test records of the staff receiving training should be kept. The data management, including computer software, should be updated in order to improve traceability of the raw data and avoid any possibility of manipulation of obtained test results. With regard to the control of the particle size, the instructions for sample homogenisation of the laboratory samples should be improved in those laboratories were this has not yet been carried out. The provisions for complete homogenisation of the sample amount as required by Council Directive 98/53/EC should be made. The laboratories should obtain an accreditation related to the method used for the determination of aflatoxin in groundnuts. The Enzyme Linked Immune Assay and the High Pressure Liquid Chromatography methods should be validated by the laboratories concerned in order to estimate the qualitative and quantitative performance characteristics. A common approach on the acceptance of a lot or sub-lot should be established. Exact criteria for the confirmation of Enzyme Linked Immune Assay results by the High Pressure Liquid Chromatography method should be established taking into account analytical uncertainties. Comparison data between the results of the Enzyme Linked Immune Assay the High Pressure Liquid Chromatography methods should be produced to establish the relationship between the aflatoxin B1 content and the total aflatoxin content in groundnuts.

The Greek Authorities should take the appropriate corrective measures to ensure the proper interpretation of the European legislation as regards TSE epidemio- surveillance in order to ensure a uniform application of community rules.
The CCA should take measures to ensure the awareness of farmers with regard to TSE, by ensuring the transmission of adequate documentation to the farmers.

The Greek Authorities should improve the training of official staff and the PVPs, taking into consideration the necessity to improve the targeting of the courses to the real needs of the staff and practitioners;

The Greek Authorities should extend compulsory notification to include TSE suspects and not only confirmed cases, and should take measures to enforce the compulsory use of the form gathering clinical and epidemiological information on TSE suspects.

The Greek Authorities should take measures to ensure that staff in laboratories and on farms consider the ruling out of TSE as an obligatory step in standard procedures to ensure that no under-estimation or under-notification of TSE takes place.
The Greek Authorities should take measures to ensure the full involvement of the slaughterhouses in TSEs surveillance activities.
The Greek authorities should take measures to ensure the proper evaluation of all clinical symptoms of cattle in the light of Commission Decision 98/272/EC.

The Greek authorities should take measures to implement an ongoing programme of monitoring of the performance of all the parties involved in TSE controls (training activities, the monitoring programme, TSE suspicions and the laboratories' activities) taking into account that the information from the PVS, LVS and PVPs is available to improve the overview of the surveillance programme.
The Greek authorities should implement clear procedures in collaboration with the National Reference Laboratory to ensure proper administrative management and handling of all samples received

recommendations.text: To prepare at central and prefectural level, detailed manuals of operation on how to respond to disease emergencies. These manuals should take account of the findings and conclusions of this mission and in particular, the experience gained by the veterinary services during the 2000 FMD outbreaks.
To improve the operation of official controls to resolve the problems seen concerning farm registration, animal identification and movement control.

To include in the proposed series of training seminars, a) specific information on the disease contingency plans and reinforce this with simulation exercises at field level and b) training on humane methods of killing for disease control purposes.

To ensure that there is a clear documented rationale for the laboratory tests performed and proper labelling of sampling material. Provision should be made to use the free diagnostic capacity (within the official laboratories) in the event of a disease outbreak. A plan describing the actions taken or planned to address the above conclusions and recommendations, including appropriate deadlines, should be submitted to the Commission services within two months of receipt of the final report. ADDENDUM Competent Authority's response to the draft report In its letter dated 2 July 2002 responding to the draft report, the competent authority made comprehensive comments which have where possible been included in the text of the report. In particular, they describe actions that have been/or will be taken in response to the recommendations of this report: 9.1.1 The current contingency plan for FMD was drastically amended and largely expanded immediately following the outbreak of FMD in 2000 and incorporates all field experience gained in combating the disease. Furthermore, in the light of recommendations made by the FVO team, more input will be invited from Regional Veterinary Services under the subsidiary principle with a view to enhance prompt and efficient implementation under specific local conditions. 9.1.2 The issue of farm registration and animal identification is being addressed by the competent Department within the DG of Veterinary Services, which is different from the Department of Infectious Diseases. 19 9.1.3 Both items are included in the syllabus of the seminars and will be 9.1.4 amplified in future courses. Labelling of sampling material with the expiry date has been effected immediately following the mission, while there are plans for improving overall laboratory facilities, including storage capacity, in both the FMD institute and the National Reference Laboratory for CSF in Athens. 20

During the supervision, the CA should also pay attention to the food safety aspects of the eggs produced in the farms. 5.1.1.3.Approval of establishments

When approving new egg packing centres or egg product establishments, the relevant CA should be able to base their decision on more detailed inspection reports in order to making the system more auditable. They should not approve centres or establishments with lay-out or equipment failures.

The approval of egg product establishments should explicitly include an approval by the CA of the pasteurisation equipment, unless such approval is provided in a more general way for a certain equipment or installation. In particular, they should impose that pasteurisers are provided with the prescribed device for the recording of the correct functioning of the safety system. 5.1.1.4.Supervision of egg packing centres and egg product establishments

Means/tools for achieving harmonised inspection/control practices should be developed and used and inspections/controls should be fully documented. 18 In their response to the draft report, the Greek Authorities have forwarded comments upon this point. 13

The CA should carry out a special investigation concerning the destination of eggs and egg products unfit for human consumption and take the necessary action in cases where irregularities are discovered.

Egg product establishments should consider increasing the number of Salmonella checks on the final product. 5.1.1.7. Trade in eggs and egg products - Trace back

Any deficiencies in regard to labelling of eggs and egg products should be rectified. 19 which imposes certain criteria for the concentration of organic acids in egg products 14 5.1.2. General recommendation The CCA should inform the Commission of the measures taken in regard to the improvement of the food safety controls within 2 months after the receipt of the final report, except for the recommendations under points 5.1.1.4, (8), (b), and 5.1.1.6, (10), (c) for which the delay of 2 months is starting from the receipt of the draft report. audits.title: Vegetable oil production and controls on PAH (Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons) contamination of such oils

recommendations.text: The Central Competent Authorities of EFET and the General State Chemical Laboratory should agree on a harmonised policy for the recall of contaminated product from the market.

The Central Competent Authorities of EFET and the General State Chemical Laboratory should agree on a harmonised policy for the handling and reprocessing of contaminated product, which has been recalled from the market. In particular the competent authority should adhere to Article 2.2 of Council Regulation (EEC) No. 315/93 laying down Community procedures for contaminants in food and ensure that levels of contaminants are kept as 16 low as possible by ensuring that producers of pomace oil follow best practice.
The reaction time from initial alerts from he rapid alert system for foods to the actual inspection of the establishment concerned should be improved.
The competent authorities should ensure that laboratories, which perform official control, are accredited to ISO/EN 17025, as required by Art 3 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC.

The General State Chemical Laboratory, and in particular the food division section of the designated laboratory for PAH analysis should ensure that the database used is complete in terms of results for individual samples.

The competent authorities should ensure that Guides to Good Hygiene Practice, which are currently under development, contain references to the critical control points in the refining of olive pomace oil, concerning the removal of PAH contamination. A programme in response to these recommendations should be produced by the Competent Authority, which should provide detailed information of the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed within 2 Months of receipt of the final report. 17 ADDENDUM Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report. This guide covers procedures and practices for handling any PAH- contaminated pomace oil. (2) With regard to point 9.1 (6) the Competent Authorities stated that the above mentioned Guide describes the critical points in the refining of olive pomace oil, and the preventive measures required to avoid contamination with PAHs. 18

recommendations.text: The competent authorities should resolve the outstanding problems of overlapping responsibility between EFET and the other central and local services. Legislation

The competent authorities should draft forward plans on the nature and frequency of the inspections to be carried out as required under Article 14.1 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC.
Monitoring programmes for official control of food hygiene should include food of non-animal origin. On site control visits
Officials carrying out official control should have adequate protective clothing and equipment.
The competent authorities should ensure adequate co-ordination at local level between services. Enforcement
The competent authorities should ensure that current transposed EU legislation is implemented by all responsible official control services.
The competent authorities should implement a single system of sanctions for official control of foodstuffs.

The competent authority should ensure returns are forwarded to Commission from all services, concerning information on the implementation during the previous year regarding the number and type of inspections, as required under Article 14.2 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC.

All services involved in official control should develop plans for the enforcement of the implementation food safety systems based on HACCP principles by food business operators, as required under Article 3 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC requires the implementation of certain HACCP principals by all food business operators. To apply the bulk milk ELISA consistently throughout the country as the screening test for dairy herds. To the Commission Services (1) To continue to monitor progress of the bovine brucellosis eradication programme in Greece. audits.title: Controls over Athens central meat market and assessment of a complaint in relation to a slaughterhouse in the Preveza region

audits.title: Brucella melitensis eradication and milk and milk products

recommendations.text: To supply the Commission services with a complete list of Greek milk-processing establishments that are deemed not to be compliant with EU legislation.

To take appropriate measures to ensure that only milk processing establishments that comply with all aspects of EU legislation are permitted to process milk-based products for placing on the market in the EU.
To enforce controls to ensure that all milk from sheep and goat holdings is pasteurised and that milk from infected animals is not processed for human consumption in approved establishments.
To ensure that the heat treatment required by Council Decision 90/242/EEC for milk from Brucella-infected animals is performed and that the produced cheese is safe for human consumption.

To submit reliable data on the actual number of dairy holdings with bovines, sheep and goats in Greece, that deliver milk to milk processing establishments to which Council Directive 92/46/EEC applies.

To take action in order: ­ to ensure that adequate quality control systems are implemented in all laboratories producing results in the framework of Annex B, Chapter II of Council Directive 92/46/EEC, ­ to ensure coverage of all holdings of all species delivering milk to milk-processing establishments, ­ to ensure that raw milk that is not in compliance with the provisions of Council Directive 92/46/EEC is not processed in approved milk processing establishments.

To submit a complete list of laboratories for official control of foodstuffs with a specification of their activities and a timetable for their accreditation. 17 Brucella melitensis eradication and control programme.
To find rapid solutions to the ongoing staff shortages and the demands placed upon them.
To take urgent action in order to introduce the new identification system for small ruminants.

To put in place corrective actions with regard to shortcomings identified with farm registers and movement controls. To clarify with the Prefectures that all holdings should be registered, irrespective of size.
To accelerate progress with the eradication programme on the Islands and to ensure that all Prefectures on the Islands apply the suspended M4 status correctly.
To ensure that the CFT test, when used as confirmatory test, is performed as required by EU legislation.
To ensure that the Prefectures submit reliable data on the numbers of holdings and any other data relating to the eradication programme, to enable a sound statistical analysis.
To maintain the progress made so far in the vaccination programme and to ensure that complete data on serological testing and slaughter of males are collected in all Prefectures on the mainland.

To ensure that the remaining Prefectures to use the software for the monthly reporting on the vaccination programme. The Greek authorities should submit an action plan to the Commission Services indicating the steps taken or planned to address the above conclusions and recommendations within 1 month of receipt of the translated final report. 9.2. To the Commission Services 9.2.1. To continue to monitor progress of the eradication/control programmes, and to review future plans in the light of the action plan submitted by the Greek authorities. 10. ADDENDUM Competent authority response to the draft mission report: In letters dated 27/02/03 and 03/03/03, the Greek Competent Authority responded to the draft report with some factual corrections and comments. Furthermore, the Greek Competent Authority indicated the actions taken to address some of the above recommendations. Recommendation 9.1.3: the CCA stated that milk from Brucella-infected animals was not brought into approved establishments. 18 Recommendation 9.1.8: the CCA stated their plans to hire 420 seasonal staff for the execution of the eradication programmes in 2003 and 30 permanent staff at central level and in the laboratories. They also stated that the Prefectural Administrative Authorities had plans to recruit new permanent staff in 2003. Recommendations 9.1.9 and 9.1.10: the CA noted the advanced status of the draft legislation which will introduce the new identification system for small ruminants, create a new model of the farm register, a central database for which data entry will be finalised by end of June 2003 and a system of checks on 10% of holdings. Furthermore, all holdings will be registered irrespective of their size. Recommendation 9.1.11: the CCA stated that necessary action will be taken to ensure correct application of M4 status of sheep/goat holdings. However, the Greek CA commented on the fact that EU-legislation does not specify the length of period during which a holding can remain in the M4 suspended status, and hence, some Prefectures had classified such holdings back to M1 status. Recommendation 9.1.12: the NRL had already acted upon this matter. Nonetheless, the CA noted the difficulties in applying the CFT test to a large number of samples, as required by EU-legislation, and therefore urged the need for adopting new serological tests for small ruminants in EU legislation. Recommendation 9.1.13: the CCA said they will provide further training to ensure correct recording of data at Prefectural level. Recommendations 9.1.14 and 9.1.15: the CCA undertook to comply fully with the issues raised. Finally, the Greek CA noted that the final report would be sent to all Prefectural (Nomos) Veterinary Services for their information and required action in relation to the recommendations in the report. 19

recommendations.text: The competent authorities should resolve the outstanding problems of overlapping of responsibilities between EFET and the other central and local services to ensure adequate official control. Legislation

The competent authorities should ensure the circulation of Good Hygiene Practice Guides in the relevant sectors of the food industry. Laboratory Services

The competent authorities should co-ordinate official control laboratories concerning the scope of this mission, in particular the designation of official control laboratories and the scope of accreditation for these laboratories.

The competent authorities should ensure that laboratories, which perform official controls, comply with the general criteria laid down in ISO/EN 17025, as required by Article 3 of Council Directive 93/99/EEC. Organisation of Controls

The competent authorities should draft forward plans on the nature and frequency of the inspections to be carried out as required under Article 14.1 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC. Training of the Competent Authority Staff
The competent authorities should ensure that staff at prefecture level receives adequate training in HACCP. Enforcement

The competent authorities should ensure that all competent authorities in all regions and prefectures enforce transposed Community legislation, in particular the enforcement of the implementation of food safety systems based on HACCP principles by food business operators, as required under Article 3 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC.

recommendations.text: To fully implement Council Directive 96/43/EC without delay;
To take action to ensure that the annual NRCP and the results of the previous year's NRCP are submitted to the Commission Services within the deadlines specified in Council decision 96/23/EC;

To ensure a more even spread of sample collection for each analyte throughout the year;
To take action to reduce the times between sample collection and availability of confirmed results in order to facilitate effective follow-up of non- complaint results;
To ensure that the targeted approach is used for collection of samples under the NRCP and that all sampling is unforeseen and unexpected;
To ensure that staff carrying out sampling are instructed to take suspect samples when appropriate; 21
To ensure that all samples collected under the NRCP are stored, sealed and transported in such a way as to ensure sample security at all stages between collection and receipt at the laboratory;
To improve the system of central monitoring and control over the sampling activities carried out by the Prefectural Veterinary Directorates;
To provide sufficient staff and appropriate equipment to ensure that all analytes included in the NRCP are analysed as planned;
To ensure that the consumables necessary for the laboratories to carry out analyses under the NRCP can be obtained as required;
To ensure that all laboratories carrying out analyses for the NRCP become accredited to ISO 17025 within the shortest possible timeframe;
To validate all methods of analyses for A Group substances to the standards required in Commission Decision 2002/657/EC within the shortest possible timeframe;

To develop an action plan to ensure that all analyses for B Group substances will be validated to the standards required in Commission Decision 2002/657/EC within the deadlines specified in that Decision;

To ensure that all laboratories carrying out analyses under the NRCP implement quality assurance measures necessary to ensure the reliability of analytical results, as foreseen in Commission Decision 2002/657/EC;
To provide sufficient resources to ensure that the NRLs can fulfil all requirements as laid out in Article 14 of Council Directive 96/23/EC;
To ensure that sufficient finance is available to allow laboratory staff to receive adequate training and, in particular, to ensure that NRL staff can always participate in relevant CRL workshops;
To ensure that only VMPs with active substances included in either Annexes I, II or III of Council Regulation (EEC) No 2377/90 are authorised for use in food producing animals;
To ensure that an updated list of all authorised VMPs is available to the relevant competent authorities and all persons involved in distribution, prescription or dispensing of VMPs;

To ensure that manufacturing of medicated feedingstuffs takes place in accordance with the requirements of Council Directive 90/167/EC. 9. These may be summarised as follows: With regard to the structure in place for the handling of ABP and other animal products not intended for human consumption 1. A political decision has been taken to reject the tender process for private bids to assume responsibility for the management of ABP in Greece in favour of promoting investment in the development of infrastructure for the handling and processing of ABP through the third Community Support Framework and the Development Act of the Ministry of Rural Development and Food and the Ministry of Economics and Finance, respectively. The proposals submitted under these two programmes been prioritised. Some of the plants are already operating and the others are expected to commence operations at the end of June 2006. With regard to the Competent Authorities 2. A number of recruitment competitions are on-going which are anticipated to lead to a net increase of 196 permanent veterinarians in the CA. The Supervision and Control Directorate carried out an on-the-spot inspection (No 306175 of 7 November 2005) on the handling of ABP in the PVS. It has planned to carry out further inspections concerning the handling of ABP in 2006. 4. Steps have been taken to increase the level of awareness of the ABP Regulation through the provision of training for 57 officials of the PVS. The course which ran from 21 November to 9 December 2005 concerned the handling of ABP, issuing of approvals and the monitoring of all agencies and other parties involved in the ABP chain. A series of seminars are being scheduled which will ensure all veterinary directorates will have staff specialised in the handling and monitoring of ABP. audits.title: Animal Welfare standards on pig and laying hen farms

recommendations.text: The necessary staff are provided, as required by Article 26 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, for official controls of animal welfare on farms.
The staff performing checks are appropriately trained, as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Verification of the effectiveness of inspections, as required by Article 8.3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, is carried out to ensure the quality and consistency of controls of animal welfare on farms.
Sufficient arrangements are made to provide training courses for pig stockpersons, as required by Article 5a of Directive 91/630/EEC.

All laying hen farms covered by the scope of Directive 99/74/EC are correctly registered and that the register is updated when there are changes to the data, as required by Article 1 of Directive 2002/4/EC, in particular the maximum capacity of the establishment.
Eggs placed on the market are appropriately marked, as required by Article 8.2 of Regulation (EC) No 2295/2003.

The risks that influence animal welfare on farm are identified and are taken into account when controls are carried out, as required by Article 3.1 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and the frequency for inspection of selected farms is appropriate.

Appropriate documented procedures, as required by Article 8.1 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, are provided so that all the requirements of Directive 91/630/EEC and Directive 99/74/EC are adequately covered during inspections.

All laying hen farms which fall within the scope of Directive 99/74/EC meet the requirements of this Directive, in particular that the height and slope of cages meet the requirements of Article 5.1(4)(5) of Directive 99/74/EC. 14
All pig holdings built or rebuilt from 1.1.2003 provide group housing of sows, as required by points 4(a) and 9 of Article 3 of Directive 91/630/EEC.
When non-compliances are detected, appropriate actions are taken so that the operator remedies the situation, as required by Article 54 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
In the whole territory the CA carries out inspections for checking compliance with the provisions of Article 7 of Directive 91/630/EEC and as by Article 8 of Directive 99/74/EC regarding laying hens.

Reports required by Decision 2000/50/EC accurately reflect the inspections carried out. 9. To ensure that control and verification procedures foreseen by Article 8 (1) and (3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2204 are applied in the field of surveillance of BT, (documented procedure for official controls and their verification).

To ensure that a history of compliance exists for setting the frequency of physical 11 checks on imports of additives as required by Art. 16.2 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. 12 To carry out appropriate official controls to ensure compliance with the rules concerning undesirable substances as laid down in Directive 2002/32/EC. audits.title: Salmonella risk in the table egg sector

recommendations.text: The sampling method applied in breeding flocks and laying flocks should comply fully 2. with Community requirements in Regulations (EC) Nos 1003/2005 and 1168/2006, correcting all deficiencies mentioned in this report. The CA should ensure that a proper sampling protocol is applied in laying hen flocks when SE or ST is detected in a holding in accordance with point 2.1. (d) of the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1168/2006. 5. 6. The CCA should gather the necessary information in order to carry out an adequate review and evaluation of the SNCPs in line with Article 5.3.d of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. The CA should ensure that the potential causes of the outbreaks are, as far as possible, studied and documented in the epidemiological investigations of outbreaks, as required by Article 8.2 of Directive 2003/99/EC. The CA should ensure that all laboratories involved in the SNCPs are designated by the CA, apply quality assurance systems and regularly participate in proficiency testing, particularly on faecal material, in line with Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. This proficiency testing should be organised or coordinated by the NRL. The CA should ensure that official samples within the SNCPs are analysed in laboratories accredited in accordance with Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and taking into account the derogation provided for in Article 18 of Regulation (EC) No 2076/2005.

audits.title: Import/transit control system and border inspection posts

recommendations.text: To take measures to clearly assign competences for checks on accompanied pet animals under Regulation (EC) No 998/2003 in order to implement the requirements of Art. 4 (1) of Regulation 882/2004.

To take measures to provide sufficient staff at central level in order implement fully the requirements of Art. 4 (c) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and to be in a position to implement verification activities, training and development of documented procedures for BIP staff as required. To review staff at the BIP of Piraeus in light of the findings of this mission and any changes in personnel brought about by listing of new BIPs.

To develop an ongoing training programme for BIP staff in order to address the issues identified in this report under point 5.3 and to better implement Art. 6 (a) and (b) of Regulation 882/2004. Where Customs are involved in official controls within the scope of this mission to ensure they are provided with appropriate training also.

To take measures to ensure that the corrective actions recommended in audits carried out under Art. 4 (6) of Regulation 882/2004 are implemented. To further take measures to implement formal procedures for verification activities by the CCA and to immediately develop a programme of inspections in order to fully implement Art. 8 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To expedite the development of the joint Ministerial Decree foreseen between MRDF and Customs in order to address the issues relating to access to information in Customs electronic systems foreseen in Art. 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004, and implementation of Art. 24 (2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 in free zones.

To further develop manuals and instructions to include guidance on checks on live mals and accompanied pet animals and guidance in relation to animal welfare uirements and to review the existing manual as necessary in light of the findings er point 5.3 of this report especially 5.3.2 and 5.3.4 in order to better apply Art. 8 of ulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To provide updated guidance to the BIPs in relation to the documents to be maintained in the BIPs in order to fulfil the requirements of point 3 of the Annex to Commission Decision 2001/812/EC and to consider if further training in this issue is required in lower throughput BIPs.
To develop a monitoring plan for imported consignments in accordance with the requirements of point 1 of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

To put in place a system in all BIPs to ensure there is proper communication between local Customs and BIP to be assured that all exiting transit consignments are presented for the checks required under Art. 11 of Directive 97/78/EC.

To develop a system so that animal health risks are taken into account by Customs officials when carrying out checks on passenger luggage in the framework of Regulation (EC) No 206/2009 in order to better implement Art. 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To take measures to correct the structural shortcomings in the BIPs of Evzoni and Neos-Kafkassos in order to comply with the requirements of Commission Decision 2001/812/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC.
To take measures to correct the minor operational shortcomings noted in all the BIPs visited in order to comply with the requirements of Commission Decision 2001/812/EC.
To provide immediate assurances that the BIP of Idomeni will no longer be used for checks on animal products for which it is not approved.
Ensure that CAs carry out official controls regularly, on a risk basis and with appropriate frequency in line with Article 3(1) and Article 15(1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that the required Common Document for checks performed on foodstuffs covered by Commission Decision 2006/504/EC is used (Annex III) in line with its Article 1(7).

Ensure that the area available for unloading and sampling of consignments is adequately covered in line with Article 4(2)(c) of Commission Decision 2006/504/EC and Article 16(3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that, in the case of non-compliant consignments for import that are to be re- dispatched, the CAs follow Article 21(1)(a) and (b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that official controls include the assessment of HACCP principles (Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) as set out in Article 10(2)(d) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that all designated laboratories comply with Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, or are availing of the derogation provided for in Article 18 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 2076/2005.
Ensure that rejections of imported consignments are always immediately notified to the Commission under the RASFF system, in accordance with Article 50(3)(c) of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002.

audits.title: Plant Health - import controls; protected zones; Rhynchophorus ferrugineus; Bursaphelenchus xylophilus; and outstanding issues in the potato sector

recommendations.text: Points of entry authorised for unloading of oak (Quercus L.) logs from the United States of America are equipped with fumigation colour reaction tests, to be able to carry out inspections as required by Article 4(2)(c) of Commission Decision 2005/359/EC.
Points of entry have access to appropriate inspection facilities, in particular moisture meters, as specified in paragraph 1, fourth indent of the Annex to Directive 98/22/EC.

Import control inspections are adapted in light of EC interceptions to address new plant health risks as required by the Annex, point (1) last indent of Directive 98/22/EC. This should include laboratory testing for latent infection at least of a portion of a consignment, which has been identified as presenting a new risk.

Points of entry authorised to receive potatoes from Egypt under derogation of Commission Decision 2004/4/EC are provided with the official list of "approved pest- free areas" prepared by the Commission, as stipulated in Article 2 of this Decision.

Notifications of interception are made available to the Commission and other Member States within two days, or preferably sooner in the case of a refusal, as required by Article 2(1) of Commission Directive 94/3/EC.
A letter of authority, which is issued for imports of the material under Commission Directive 2008/61/EC, is always compliant with the model set out by Article 2(2) of this Directive.

Premises and facilities, where activities under derogations of Commission Directive 2008/61/EC are carried out, are appropriately identified, as required by Annex I of this Directive, point 2(a), fourth indent.

Regular and systematic official surveys for the presence of organisms in respect of which Greece has been recognised as a protected zone based on Commission Regulation (EC) No. 690/2008, are organised and conducted, as required by Article 2(1)(h) of Directive 2000/29/EC and as specified by Directive 92/70/EEC.
A system of recording and keeping of survey results is developed, as required by the third indent of Article 1(3)(a) of Directive 92/70/EEC. 40

The survey methodology and conduct are notified to the Commission as required by Article 1(3)(d) of Directive 92/70/EEC, and the results of the surveys are notified to the Commission as required by Article 2(1)(h) of Directive 2000/29/EC.

Regulated articles listed in Annex V, Part A, Section II to Council Directive 2000/29/EC, for which Greece has protected zone status, are moved within Greece accompanied by a valid Protected Zone (ZP) plant passport, to comply with Article 10(2) of the same Directive.

Occasional official checks on regulated articles being moved into or within the Protected Zone are organised, as required by Article 12(1) of Directive 2000/29/EC, to ensure compliance with the Directive, in particular with Article 10(2) of the same Directive.
In cases where Rhynchophorus ferrugineus is found, the control measures are imposed according to Annex II to Commission Decision 2007/365/EC.

In case of findings of Ralstonia solanacearum, the extent of probable contamination is determined in accordance with Article 5(1)(a)(iii) of Council Directive 98/57/EC, and any plant material determined as probably contaminated is disposed of as specified in Article 6(2) of the same Directive.

In case of findings of Ralstonia solanacearum, the extent of the contamination is determined in accordance with Article 5(1)(a)(i) of Council Directive 98/57/EC, in particular that surface water is considered as an element in the investigation, as specified in Annex IV of the same Directive.

Official surveys for Bursaphelenchus xylophilus are conducted, as required by Article 4(1) of Commission Decision 2006/133/EC, on susceptible wood and bark and susceptible plants originating in Greece, to determine whether there is any evidence of infestation by this pest. The results of those surveys are notified to the other Member States and the Commission annually by 15 December, as required by the same Article.

Official surveys for Phytophthora ramorum in Greece are conducted, as required by Article 6(1) of Commission Decision 2002/757/EC. The results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and to the other Member States by 1 November of each year, as required by Article 6(2) of the same Decision. 41

Official surveys for the presence of Diabrotica virgifera in areas in Greece, where maize is grown, are conducted, as required by Article 2(1) of Commission Decision 2003/766/EC. The results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and to the other Member States by 31 December of each year, as required by Article 2(2) of the same Decision.

Official surveys on premises involved in the production of tomato plants and tomato fruits, for the presence of Pepino mosaic virus, are conducted in Greece, as required by Article 4 of Commission Decision 2004/200/EC, and the results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and to the other Member States.

Official surveys for the presence of Dryocosmus kuriphilus in Greece are conducted, as required by Article 5(1) of Commission Decision 2006/464/EC, and the results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and to the other Member States by 31 December of each year.

Official surveys, and where appropriate, testing, for the presence of Potato spindle tuber viroid on host plants, or evidence of infection by this harmful organism, are conducted in Greece, as required by Article 3(1) of Commission Decision 2007/410/EC. The results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and the other Member States.

Official surveys for the presence of Gibberella circinata in Greece are conducted, as required by Article 5(1) of Commission Decision 2007/433/EC, and the results of those surveys are notified to the Commission and to the other Member States by 15 December of each year. The Single Authority in Greece is recommended to consider:
Carrying out more systematic and frequent inspections of cargo with Wood Packaging Material, including random sampling even in the absence of symptoms or signs of infection or infestation.

Increasing the use of pheromone traps when carrying out the surveys prescribed by Article 5(1) of Commission Decision 2007/365/EC, and when establishing a pest free area as prescribed in Annex I, Point 2(b), to the same Decision.
Ensure that a multi-annual national control programme for pesticide residues is established as required by Article 30 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 396/2005.
Ensure that the national control programme for pesticide residues in place contains at least the information listed in Article 30 (1) (a), (b), (c) and (d).

Ensure that official controls are carried out at all appropriate stages of production, processing and distribution, as required by Article 3 (3) of Regulation (EC) 882/2004 and consider that samples within the national control programme for pesticide residues are taken as close to the point of supply as is reasonable to allow for any subsequent enforcement action to be taken, as set out in Article 27(1) of Regulation (EC) No 396/2005.
Ensure that a documented procedure is in place in the case of sampling for pesticide residues as laid down in Article 8 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

The CCA should take action to ensure that the level of official controls on transport can be realistically planned and effectively implemented as required in Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 where it requires that official controls are carried out regularly, on a risk basis and with appropriate frequency. In this regard, the CCA should consider collecting and utilising best practice from Regional Units and involving them in any future proposals.

In conjunction with planned actions to address recommendation No.1, the CCA should ensure that when controls on journey logs are carried out, as required in Article 15(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005, they are carried out by trained staff. The CCA should consider the targeting of such controls using information available in the TRACES database in each Regional Unit to peform an initial screening of the type and volume of trade entering and leaving the regional unit using a desk based exercise and then targeting different types of transport according to the local risk criteria set. For this purpose, consideration could be given to the verification of transporters' compliance with requirements in Chapter V of Annex 1 of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 by requesting satellite navigation system records, tachograph records, temperature printouts, and copies of journey logs.

The CCA should take the necessary action to provide for facilities in or in the immediate vicinity of the two main ferry ports of Igoumenitsa and Patras to enable animals to rest after unloading if required, as laid down in Annex 1, Chapter V, point 1 (7)b of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005. The CCA should notify other Member States' Transport Contact Points to ensure that local veterinary units involved in the verification of the planning sections of journey logs and the issue of TRACES certificates for consigments destined for Greece are fully aware that facilities are not presently in place for transporters using these ports. Similarly the CCA should notify all Greek transporters authorised for long distance transport of the implications for journey times relating to the lack of these facilities.

The CCA should ensure that in conjunction with actions taken to address recommendations No 1 and 2, physical inspections of the means of transport and the animals are actually carried out as required in Article 27(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005. The CA should consider collecting and utilising best practice from Regional Units and involving them in any future proposals to ensure that the best use of available resources is made e.g. combining animal health and animal welfare inspections at transporters/dealers' premises; ensuring staff trained on animal welfare and approval of vehicles are present at slaughterhouses on days intra-Union consignments are expected.

The CCA should ensure that verification of the effectiveness of official controls on animal welfare during transport and at slaughter as required in Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 is included in actions taken to address recommendations No.1,2,4, 6 and 7.

The CCA should ensure that inspections and controls in slaughterhouses are carried out in an appropriate manner to ensure the requirements of Articles 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Directive 93/119/EC are effectively implemented.

The CCA should ensure that official controls on animal welfare during transport and slaughter are effectively enforced according to the requirements of Articles 54 and 55 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. In this regard, the CCA should ensure that efficient and effective coordination and cooperation is put in place between different units carrying out official controls. To this end, improvements should be sought in the complimentary work of the public health department and the animal welfare section of the CCA and in the Regional Units regarding animal welfare at slaughter and killing. Consideration should be given to improving the sharing of information and developing synergies to enhance the enforcement of official controls e.g. at CCA level, by actively liaising with RUs in those cases where enforcement action has not been taken by the regions in slaughterhouses where animal welfare non-compliances have been identifedConsideration should be given to developing new strategies in consultation with the Regional Units to overcome the persistent lack of enforcement action.

The CCA should ensure that the implementation of the provisions of Articles 4(3) and (5) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 requiring efficient and effective coordination and cooperation between different units carrying out official controls is improved regarding the persistent under-reporting by Regional Units to the CCA of the results of official controls on animal welfare during transport and at slaughter and killing. In this regard the CCA should intensify efforts to develop a comprehensive IT reporting system for the practical input of data from the Regional Units, whilst also addressing the infrastructural problems associated with the smaller field offices' lack of equipment.

The CCA should ensure that prompt action is taken to address the deficiencies identifed in the authorisation and operational surveillance of dealers' premises throughout Greece in order to comply with the requirements of Article 13 of Directive 64/432/EEC.

recommendations.text: To ensure that the checklists used for official controls on food business operators producing meat and products thereof include within their scope the relevant requirements to comply with the provisions of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) No 931/2011, in order to ensure that food consignments are traceable and the checklists used for official controls on food business operators, producing foodstuffs for delivery to the ultimate consumer, include the relevant labelling requirements for such products laid down in Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011.

citations.text: The checklist issued by the EFET for controls in establishments producing meat and meat products thereof includes controls on general hygiene requirements, FBOs' HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) based systems and contains questions on traceability, labelling and sampling for additives. Traceability controls and the checklists used are focused on one step forward and one step backward in line with the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002. Nevertheless, in some establishments, particularly those which export products, official controls on internal traceability are effectively performed. The CCA confirmed that the checklist does not contain specific questions on the use of additives for which limits are established during manufacturing process such as nitrates and nitrites and this will be reviewed.

The checklist issued by the DGSAPVS is mainly focused on general hygiene and does not contain questions related to traceability, labelling and use of additives. However, in one establishment visited, the local CA used the EFET checklist related to traceability, but not related to labelling and use of additives. The CCA stated that this checklist will be reviewed. 5

A system of official controls is in place and performs effectively. Documented procedures are established and applied. Some checklists are not complete as they do not contain relevant questions on controls on traceability, labelling and use of additives for establishments in the case of establishments under the control of the DGSAPVS and on the use of food additives in the case of the EFET. Both CCA indicated that the checklists will be reviewed in this regard.

For the samples, in particular, for meat and products thereof, produced and traded within Greece, not all suppliers provided information in trade documents on food supplied with a reference identifying the lot, batch or consignment, as appropriate. Instead in most cases this information is retrieved on arrival by the receiving FBO from the labels attached to the meat. For the 10 cases seen, for which the authorities confirmed traceability, this has not led to an interruption of traceability within the supply chain of meat and products thereof. The labels or copies were not kept in all establishments visited. For one sample, documentation on certain ingredients used was missing (see paragraph 35 below). Documentation to verify the physical flow of the products within the establishments such as production data for reconciliation, the product recipes, the technical specifications of the additives and spice mixtures used were available apart from some ingredients (see paragraph 35 below). The observations made by the authorities regarding labelling could be confirmed, but some additional remarks were made for three cases verified on-the-spot (see paragraph 35 below). In two cases the use of food additives was not in line with the requirements of Union legislation. The amount of nitrite used in one meat product sample was in excess (157 mg/kg) and the amount of nitrite and nitrate used in another meat product sample slightly exceeded (150.2 mg/kg) the maximum amount that may be added during manufacturing and is therefore non-compliant with the requirements set out in Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 (maximum limit 150 mg/kg).

The authorities identified some minor non-compliances in the traceability and labelling that had no impact on food safety for the eleven traceable samples. The authorities did not identify some non-compliances related to the use of food additives, in particular, the use of nitrites and nitrates. The information referred to in Article 3 of Regulation (EU) No 931/2011 was not available for a particular ingredient used. 5.2.2.2.Official controls on food business operators' obligations Findings

audits.title: evaluate the official controls on consignments in transit

recommendations.text: To gather and analyse relevant information to ensure that all eligible consignments in transit are subject to veterinary checks in all the BIPs, as required by Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Articles 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004.

citations.text: The competent authority informed the audit team that none of the BIPs visited had direct access to information available in Customs contrary to the requirement of Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004 and Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 (see finding 5).

The staff at Pireas port BIP stated that they carry out manifest checks (to identify possible consignments not presented for controls at the BIPs) on an ad hoc basis. There is no record of these controls, contrary to the requirement described in the BIP manual. The road BIPs visited do not implement any checks to identify such cases, contrary to the requirements of Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004. The procedure for controls of transits described in the BIP manual does not refer to the above-mentioned requirements for the road BIPs.

The official control system of transit consignments at the entry BIPs ensures that only consignments eligible for transits are accepted as required by EU legislation with the exception of specific shortcomings on (i) the screening of available information on arriving consignments in the road BIPs that reduce the ability to detect consignments that should undergo border controls, and (ii) the identity checks, which are limited to tail checks, therefore do not ensure that the consignment tallies exactly with the description in the accompanying document. All consignments were confirmed at exit. 5.2.2 Controls at the exit Border Inspection Posts

responses.response: 1. There is a good collaboration between the Customs and the Veterinary Authorities at both central and local level. This is reflected at the Memorandum of Cooperation between the two services, the common meetings, the availability of Customs data to perform cross checks on the imported consignments. Up to now, our service has focused on receiving a direct access in the Customs database, probably due to a misinterpretation of the previous recommendations, clarified during this mission. In collaboration with Customs, our intention is to formalise a written procedure in order to be in line with articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) 136/2004 and articles 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) 282/2004. Deadline to finalise the procedure 31/05/2016. 2. In regard of this recommendation, the guidance for the controls of transits included in the BIP manual will be modified accordingly to include guidance for the road BIPs. Deadline: 31/03/2016. 3. In accordance with the BIP manual, "the check of manifests must be documented". A reminder will be sent to all BIPs until the 31/01/2016 and a follow up will be done by the CCA during the supervision visits.

citations.text: In all the BIPs visited, staff perform identity checks for all transit consignments to ascertain that the products correspond to the information given in the accompanying certificates or documents, , as required in Article 4(4) of Directive 97/78/EC. recommendations.text: To develop a system of controls for EU goods re-entering the Union after transiting via third countries, to ensure that only eligible consignments are authorised into the territory as required by Article 6(1) of Directive 89/662/EEC and Article 7(1) of Directive 90/425/EEC.

citations.text: Customs stated that all EU goods including food of animal origin and live animals arriving from third countries are always accompanied with customs documents and are subject to a Customs documentary check. There is no arrangement with the veterinary service or any instruction on what checks need to be done for the consignments of veterinary interest when these are of EU origin. The audit team noted that the competent authority is not enforcing the requirement to control EU goods re-entering from external transits as provided in Article 6(1)(a) of Directive 89/662/EEC and Article 7(1) of Directive 90/425/EEC.

The audit team found cases of Intra-trade animal health certificates (INTRA) consignments issued by Greece for which the route is not defined/entered as required in the notes for guidance for intra-Community certification in Commission Regulation (EC) No 599/2004. This hinders notification to the relevant authorities and compromises the capability of the officers at exit points to identify the consignments and perform official controls at the exit contrary to the requirements in Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 206/2010. The same appears on consignments destined to Greece certified in other Member States.

The audit team found no cases of checked consignments in external transit. It is yet unknown whether such movements exist due to the lack of controls (see finding 27) and incomplete registration of intra-trade movements in TRACES (see finding 28).
The official controls do not ensure that if there are movements of EU consignments through third countries into Greece the EU animal health requirements are met. 9

recommendations.text: To ensure that the results of previous monitoring plans are taken into account when drafting monitoring plans, as required by point 1 of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

citations.text: The monitoring plan was last made available to the BIPs and to the authorised island entry points listed in Annex I to Decision 94/641/EC in 2011. Since then it has not been reviewed/amended. The competent authority stated that this was due to a lack of human resources. In this way, the results of previous years are not taken into consideration, contrary to the requirement of paragraph 1 of Annex II to Regulation No 136/2004.

Basically in compliance with the legal requirements, there is a monitoring plan in place to be implemented at the BIPs. The plan is prepared on the basis of risk management in order to ensure that it covers all relevant commodities and the related risks. The plan has not been reviewed/amended since 2011, therefore does not take into account the results of previous monitoring or emerging risks. This means that its ability to detect hazardous goods may be compromised. 5.1.2 Implementation of the monitoring plan

responses.response: The results of the previous monitoring plans will be taken into account in the new draft which is foreseen to be finalised until 31/01/2016.

recommendations.text: To ensure that the person responsible for the consignment or its representative is liable for the costs incurred by the competent authorities for the activities of laboratory testing in case of suspicion of non-compliance as required by Article 22 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

citations.text: At the Pireas and Peplos BIPs, the cost of all laboratory tests (including those under re- enforced checks or suspicion) is covered by the State. In the other BIPs visited, depending on the laboratory in which the analysis is performed, some test costs are borne by the operators and others by the State. The cases in which economic operators are not charged for the cost of controls (e.g. sampling and testing) in case of suspicion or re-enforced checks are not in line with the requirement of Article 22 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

There is a system in place which allows BIP staff to take samples in case of suspicion. The system works correctly as per EU legislation and planned arrangements. However, the system does not ensure that the operator responsible for the consignment or its representative is liable for the costs incurred by the competent authority for the actions in case of suspicion.

responses.response: The costs of the laboratory tests performed within the scope of ties official controls are covered by the State. The decision defining the possibility of the official labs to perform testing on samples t by privates and which is foreseen in article 5, paragraph 1 of Law 2332/31-08-1995, is still pending. The CCA will address a letter to the responsible Department of the Directorate of Veterinary Care, Drugs and Extension Work to include in this draft decision the laboratory tests performed at BIP level in the framework of suspicion or reinforced checks.

recommendations.text: To gather and analyse relevant information to ensure that eligible consignments are subject to veterinary checks, as required by Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Articles 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004, as regards the Greek islands under Decision 94/641/EC.

citations.text: The memorandum of cooperation between the competent authority and Customs covers the official controls on transits. However, although it foresees the granting of access of the official veterinarians at the BIPs to the Customs database, this is not implemented. The competent authority confirmed that none of the BIPs and the LVUs visited had direct access to information available in Customs contrary to the requirement of Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. In addition, the competent authority at central level has not considered using data available in the Customs database to verify the correctness of the controls laid down in Decision 94/641/EC.

With regard to recommendation No 5 of DG SANCO 2013-6977 report, the audit included visits to the islands of Crete and Lesvos and assessment of the performance of the LVUs Iraklio and Mitilini, respectively, as regards the requirements of Decision 94/641/EC. The audit team noted the following: a. Central competent authority i. The competent authority has made available the documented procedures related to official import controls in line with Articles 6(b) and 8(1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. ii. The competent authority performed a supervision visit at the Iraklio LVU in 2013 and an internal audit at the Mitilini LVU in 2014 in line with Articles 4(6) and 8(3)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. Several deficiencies were identified during the internal audit in Mitilini (e.g. the operators that were handling imports of fresh fish from Turkey had no approved establishments). b. Iraklio LVU i. There is a pre-notification system, in line with the requirement of Article 2(1) of Regulation 136/2004/EC and Article 3, first indent, of Decision 94/641/EC. ii. A CVED accompanies the consignment to the operator's facilities. The CVED bears a red stamp, indicating that the goods are destined for consumption only on the island of Crete. iii. In one out of five establishments that import through Iraklio port, the operator stamps every carton box with the number of the CVED, and provides the buyer with an invoice that bears the stamp "only for consumption on the island of Crete" in line with the requirement of the third indent of Article 3 of Decision 94/641/EC . The importer keeps an electronic traceability system in line with the requirement of the second indent of the same Article. iv. The establishment visited had good hygiene conditions in line with the requirements of Annex 1 to Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and was approved as required by Article 6(3) of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Article 4(1) of Regulation (EC) No 853/2004. v. LVU staff perform a cross-check with cargo manifests at the port but not at the airport, contrary to the requirement of Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. vi. The competent authority stated that veterinary checks are performed at arrival in the port of Iraklio as per Article 1 of Annex II to Decision 13 94/641/EC. The LVU staff make regular inspections in the facilities as required by Article 2 of Annex II to Decision 94/641/EC, and document these in the context of supervision visits. vii. In some cases, in order to have access to the entire consignment and ensure that the sample is representative, LVU staff perform sampling under the monitoring plan at the operators' facilities (after the consignments are imported and the CVEDs are already issued). viii. In all cases examined by the audit team, the certificates of origin of the goods indicated that they were eligible for being imported to the EU. c. Mitilini LVU i. According to the competent authority, there were two importers that imported fishery products into Lesvos island, but they ceased import operations in 2013. This is confirmed in the competent authority's annual report to the EU Commission, where 2013 was the last year in which Lesvos had imports of fresh fish from Turkey (approximately 2 tonnes). ii. The files examined indicated the following: 1. There was no pre-notification system, contrary to the requirement of Article 2(1) of Regulation 136/2004/EC and Article 3, first indent, of Decision 94/641/EC. 2. The competent authority did not gather and analyse relevant information to ensure that eligible consignments are subject to veterinary checks under Decision 94/641/EC as required. 3. There was no system equivalent to the requirements of Article 3 of Decision 94/641/EC to inform purchasers that the products are for local consumption only. 4. The documentary checks required in point 1 of Annex II to Decision 94/641/EC are not effective to detect incorrect certification (e.g. consignments of fishery products from Turkey are accepted with

Recommendation No 2 from DG(SANCO)/2013-6977 is addressed. However, appropriate actions have still not been taken as regards recommendations 1 and 5 of the same report. In addition, the system does not ensure in some cases that staff at the LVUs in the Greek islands gather and analyse relevant information to ensure that eligible consignments are subject to veterinary checks under Decision 94/641/EC and that imported consignments are only handled at approved operators' facilities.

recommendations.text: To ensure the consistency of the official import controls in the BIPs in line with Article 4(4) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

citations.text: At Peplos BIP (which is the most significant in terms of import volumes): 6 i. staff do not follow the procedures laid down in the monitoring plan as regards the percentage of samples for testing (only one random sample was taken in 2014 in 3,993 consignments imported) contrary to the requirement of Article 8(1) of Regulation No 882/2004/EC. The head of the BIP stated that this is due to the lack of human resources at the BIP. The competent authority presented at the meeting at Peplos BIP the decision to appoint an additional official veterinarian to support the activities at this BIP. ii. consignments of aquaculture sea bass and sea bream from Turkey destined to several Member States (40% of all EU imports is introduced through this BIP) were tested for antimicrobial substances once in the last three years (in 2013) and the result was satisfactory. iii. consignments of casings imported from Iran were not tested in the last 3 years (the import of Iranian casings destined to the EU via this BIP is approximately 40% of total EU imports). iv. consignments of fish species under the Customs nomenclature code 03048990 were not tested in 2014 (202 consignments were imported via Peplos). The BIP staff stated that these commodities present a low risk. However, all the above- mentioned commodities rank among the 10 largest imports of products of animal origin through the Greek BIPs in terms of quantity in 2014, with the lowest of them being a total import of 3,000 tonnes. On the basis of finding 4 those commodities should have been tested.

The monitoring plan is generally implemented in accordance with the legal requirements. The BIPs are following the planned arrangements with the exception of Peplos (the most significant in terms of import volumes). Thus the capability of the plan to detect hazardous goods is compromised. This is further reduced in cases where sampling of consignments is not representative or where the facilities cannot ensure hygienic handling of samples.
